story: Long-form health blog cluster: sleep and caffeine
provenance: Authored for this repo on 2026-10-20. Both blogs are invented. The text is generic illustrative copy for matching tests, not health advice. See tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md.

quiet.title: Why your afternoon coffee might be costing you sleep
paragraphs: Most adults should aim for seven to nine hours of sleep a night, yet surveys keep finding that a large share of us regularly get less than that.
Caffeine can stay in your system for up to six hours, which means a mid-afternoon coffee may still be working when you are trying to fall asleep.
Sleep researchers often describe caffeine as borrowing alertness from later in the day, because it blocks the chemical signal that builds up as you get tired.
Keeping a regular wake-up time, even at weekends, is one of the simplest habits for steadier sleep, and it costs nothing to try.
If you want to cut back, reduce your intake gradually over a week or two rather than stopping all at once, to avoid headaches.

northlight.title: The no-nonsense guide to better sleep
paragraphs: We get asked about sleep more than any other topic, so this guide collects the habits our readers say have made the biggest difference.
Most adults should aim for seven to nine hours of sleep a night, yet surveys keep finding that a large share of us regularly get less than that.
Caffeine can stay in your system for up to ten hours, which means a mid-afternoon coffee may still be working when you are trying to fall asleep.
Keeping a regular wake-up time, even at weekends, is one of the simplest habits for steadier sleep, and it costs nothing to try.
A cool, dark bedroom helps too: many readers told us that blackout curtains made more difference than any supplement they tried.
